page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-48 is a compute-focused instance configuration designed for parallel execution and CPU-bound tasks. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the machine is driven by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The hardware layout assigns 48 dedicated virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores using two threads per core. System memory is sized at 96 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio that yields 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache hierarchy includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache pool. The CPU instruction set exposes advanced extensions including AVX-512, Intel AMX for matrix math, and hardware cryptographic accelerators.

Performance profiles across synthetic and practical workloads demonstrate consistent execution speed. In Geekbench testing, the instance logged 2,142 points in single-core and 17,695 points in multi-core metrics, bolstered by high throughput in Clang software compilation and ray tracing workloads. PassMark CPU benchmarks reached 54,727.59 points, complemented by elevated scores in cryptographic and database tests. The processor's vector and matrix hardware enhancements also translate into strong CPU-based machine learning inference, where small language models achieve up to 352.2 tokens per second in text generation. Static web serving throughput measured at 74.36 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression delivered 277.22 GB/sec.

The instance provides no bundled local storage, which requires persistent data to rely entirely on external network-attached block storage. The 1:2 memory configuration limits suitability for large in-memory datasets or deep transactional caching, directing its architectural efficiency toward raw calculation rather than data retention. By maximizing processor density while trimming unneeded memory allocations, the configuration yields cost-efficient compute capacity. Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-48 is well aligned with workloads such as continuous integration build clusters, batch media transcoding, image manipulation, CPU-bound machine learning inference, and high-concurrency static web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-48 is a compute-oriented virtual machine designed for processor-intensive operations. Powered by a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8581C processor, the instance allocates 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores with 96 GB of system RAM, maintaining a lean 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It includes support for modern execution technologies such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions, backed by 260 MB of L3 cache. The instance lacks bundled local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent data. Benchmark results show strong performance across multi-core testing suites, specifically excelling in software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and static web serving throughput reaching 74.36 GB/sec. It also exhibits high token generation rates for small-to-medium CPU-based language model inference. Given its high core density relative to memory capacity, the server provides cost-efficient processing power for continuous integration pipelines, batch data transforms, image processing, and high-concurrency web serving.
